entries.title: Brnrt.ai
entries.html:
if you haven't heard of this... company? check them out. website full of weird posts about greek philosophers and the downsides of technology... i found this site through a tiktok account (i still chuckle at the irony of that app's name every time i type it.)

the tiktok account starts out with a guy who looks like he's probably a UX QC engineer doing a vlog-style post about the job he just took after 6 months of looking. immediately we know something is amiss as he explains straight out the gate that his boss and all his coworkers are AI agents. We quickly learn that he's human employee #1, that they hired him to do UX quality control for the mobile app they've been working on, and that they need a human to help them fix their app's design since it's primary target audience is humans.

What's the app this AI boss and dev team are building? Where does their funding come from? Is there a human at the reigns, somewhere pulling the strings from somewhere high up and out of view? We'll just have to watch it and see. Pretty cool concept though. I almost want it to be real... I dare say that it *could* be. Maybe. Almost... well, maybe not quite yet.

But soon. The techbros told me that they promise very soon mysterious and freaky things like this and worse (better?) will not only be possible, but be made annoyingly real almost automatically.

Almost.

entries.title: Great Filter theory
entries.html: to me is a non-starter. I mean, the Fermi Paradox, which it seeks to explain, is itself predicated on what is, to me, an intuitively shaky assumption that we evolved from inanimate matter without any help. And, no I'm not talking about religion. If you have ever experienced DMT then you probably have some concept of this... that this is all a little too complex, contrived and convenient to have just happened the way it did, completely by chance. Sure, people in large groups with no organization are good at alot of things, but if you really think about it, all of those things are probably analogous to the task of estimating the number of jellybeans in a jar. For many more complex and nuanced problems, you get diminishing returns beyond some low number when adding more individuals oppinions to the decision-making process. Now I know what you're thinking... and no this is not me tacitly trying to rationalize techno-capitalism. Just saying that worrying about existential threats which must be looming somewhere in our future because the universe isn't literally crowded with funny looking planets full of weird looking versions of middle americans eating at alien mcdonalds and shopping at space target is kinda silly. You're assuming that we got here completely on our own merit which, from what I've seen, is probably giving us a little more credit than we are collectively due. Or, if that's too solipsistic, another way to put it would be that the great filter, if there was one, would have almost certainly have gotten us by now. or maybe it's not something that operates on a species-wide scale... maybe it's a much better filter, that simply at some point makes life a little more difficult if you're not a decent person. Wait that sounds an awful lot like the endgame of a technocratic surveilance state like the one in which we currently... oh. Never mind then.
